case_name: State of Gujarat and Another v Vaghela Dayabhai Chaturbhai and Others
facts: These five appeals by certificate are preferred by the State of Gujarat against the common judgment dated April 25/28, 1969 delivered in five petitions u/art.

The expression 'bhatha land' means land which forms part of the bed of a river on which vegetables, melon, cucumber etc. can be grown during the lean period after the rainy season is over when the level of the water in the river is quite low.

Till the year 1951, the cultivation rights over bhatha lands in the area in question were being disposed of by public auction and the successful bidders were being treated as lessees of the lands for short periods.
In the year 1964 however, lease-hold rights over bhatha lands were disposed of on eksal basis by public auction.
The State Government passed the following Resolution in supersession of all existing orders:--

Thereafter twenty-two members belonging to Waghari Harijan community were granted lease-hold rights in respect of a bhatha land for a period of ten years pursuant to the above Government Resolution by the Collector of Ahmedabad on July 18, 1967.

The petitioners in Special Civil Application No. 1079 of 1967 which was one of the writ petitions out of which these appeals arise questioned the validity of the Government Resolution dated December 28, 1966 and the order of the Collector granting the lease dated July 18, 1967 in favour of the said twenty- two persons.
issues: The constitutional validity of the Resolution of the Government of Gujarat bearing No. L.B.B. 3964/101585-C dated December 28, 1966
Whether the grants made by the Collector on the basis of the impugned Resolution were ultra vires the scheme of the Code and violative of Art. 14 of the Constitution
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners alleged that some of them were in possession of portions of the lands which had been disposed of by the order of the Collector by virtue of the eksal tenures created in their favour under auctions held in or about the year 1964 and they could not be dispossessed without following the procedure prescribed by section 79-A read with s. 202 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code')

They contended that the Government Resolution dated December 28, 1966 and the grants made by the Collector on the basis of the said Resolution were liable to be struck down on the ground that they were violative of Art. 14 of the Constitution
respondent_arguments: The State Government and the other respondents in the writ petitions resisted the petitions
They contended that the grants made by the Collector on the basis of the impugned Resolution were valid and did not violate any provision of the Code or the Constitution
court_reasoning: After hearing the parties, the High Court quashed the Government Resolution and the grants made by the Collector holding that they were ultra vires the scheme of the Code and were also violative of Art. 14 of the Constitution
holding: The High Court quashed the Government Resolution and the grants made by the Collector
